page: Microsoft Azure E48bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 Intel processors and provisioned via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 48 dedicated vCPUs paired with 384.0 GB of memory, which establishes an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This allocation structure suits computational processes that require extensive system memory per processing thread while maintaining dedicated vCPU execution without resource contention.

From an input and output perspective, the E48bs_v6 includes no onboard local disk storage and features zero graphics processing units. Storage operations are handled exclusively through attached remote block storage, with native support for Azure Premium Storage to achieve high block storage throughput. Network interfaces do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual network routing mechanisms for external connectivity.

Architecturally, the absence of local disks reduces host-level failure exposure but requires adequate provisioning of external storage resources to meet disk I/O demands. The hardware profile exhibits strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise software by consolidating high RAM volume into a single instance without the financial footprint of attached hardware accelerators. Optimal workloads include in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning platforms, distributed caching systems, and large relational database management engines.
description: Microsoft Azure E48bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture, managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of system memory, maintaining a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It contains no onboard local storage and includes zero GPUs, relying entirely on attached Premium Storage remote block devices for persistent and non-persistent disk operations. Designed within the Ebsv6 series to deliver elevated block storage performance, the instance balances extensive RAM capacity with dedicated compute allocation. Given its substantial memory capacity and remote storage orientation, the instance operates cost-effectively for large-scale enterprise software that demands high memory density without the overhead of unused physical accelerators. Appropriate deployment scenarios include large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, large-scale data analytics, and memory-bound transactional caching clusters requiring predictable dedicated execution.
